subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this custom cooperative glob walker and bootstrap-hook scheduling as the bounded fix for bootstrap-context stalls despite possible extra-bootstrap ordering, prompt-byte, and handler-timing changes?
rationale: The patch addresses the measured P1 hot path without expanding public API, but bootstrap file selection and hook sequencing are compatibility-sensitive agent-context surfaces whose upgrade tradeoff requires owner intent.

options.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
options.body: Accept the internal compatibility tradeoff, rebase onto current main, rerun focused and SDK-surface gates, and land the bounded bootstrap fix.

options.title: Require Connected Runtime Proof
options.body: Keep the implementation shape but require a current-head embedded run showing channel or timer responsiveness during a slow bootstrap before merging.

options.title: Pause For Broader Architecture
options.body: Do not land this branch if owners prefer worker isolation, priority scheduling, or caching rather than maintaining a custom glob implementation.

recommendation.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
recommendation.body: Accept the internal compatibility tradeoff, rebase onto current main, rerun focused and SDK-surface gates, and land the bounded bootstrap fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest merged history spans the internal hook architecture, bootstrap hooks, and guarded workspace-reading boundary affected by the decision.
